figures.name: fig01_inventory_status
figures.title: Dataset inventory and processing status
figures.caption: Status of the 36 files discovered in DATAS/ (left) and volume per dataset group (right, log scale).
figures.interpretation: 23 files were processed into validated outputs, 8 validated in native form and 4 are metadata/documentation. GLIMS polygons dominate the volume (95% of 9.5 GB).

figures.name: fig02_omi_extent_timeseries
figures.title: Antarctic monthly sea-ice extent time series
figures.caption: Monthly-mean Southern Hemisphere sea-ice extent from the Copernicus Marine OMI product; orange line = mean of complete calendar years; dotted lines mark months stored as _FillValue.
figures.interpretation: Strong seasonal cycle between ~2.2 and ~20.3 million km^2. The least-squares trend of the annual mean over 1979-2024 is -0.060 million km^2 per decade; the lowest monthly value is 2.23 million km^2 (2023-02). Missing months: 1986-04, 1986-05, 1986-06, 1987-12.

figures.name: fig03_omi_extent_anomaly
figures.title: Annual sea-ice extent anomaly
figures.caption: Mean of monthly anomalies (extent minus the file's monthly climatology) for each complete year.
figures.interpretation: The three most negative years are 2023 (-1.59), 2024 (-1.06), 2017 (-0.85) million km^2; 7 of the 9 complete years since 2016 are below the long-term climatology, whereas 14 of 35 years before 2016 were.

figures.name: fig04_extent_seasonal_cycle
figures.title: Seasonal cycle of sea-ice extent
figures.caption: Monthly climatology from the CMEMS OMI file (shaded ±1 standard deviation) compared with the NSIDC Sea Ice Index daily climatologies averaged to calendar months. The Northern Hemisphere file collected in DATAS/ is shown only as a contrast (out of Antarctic scope).
figures.dataset: OMI NetCDF; NSIDC G02135 S (downloaded) and N (DATAS/) climatology CSVs
figures.interpretation: Antarctic extent peaks in September (18.83 million km^2) and is lowest in February (3.26), opposite in phase to the Arctic. NSIDC South 1981-2010 peaks at 18.49 (month 9) and bottoms at 3.07 (month 2).

figures.name: fig05_omi_vs_nsidc_difference
figures.title: OMI vs NSIDC monthly extent difference
figures.caption: Difference between CMEMS OMI monthly extent and NSIDC G02135 daily extent averaged to months (months with >=10 daily values). Products are compared, not merged.
figures.interpretation: 548 months matched; correlation r = 0.9999; mean difference +0.369 ± 0.097 million km^2 (max |diff| 0.75). The products agree closely in variability; the offset reflects different SIC algorithms and land masks.

figures.name: fig06_dmi_sic_distribution
figures.title: DMI-ASIP sea-ice concentration distribution
figures.caption: Exact counts of ice_concentration values in the 2023-02-02 DMI-ASIP mosaic (left) and classification of all 65.5 million grid cells (right). Classes are mutually exclusive.
figures.interpretation: The CNN product is quantised in 10 % steps (11 distinct valid values). Only 1.26% of the grid holds a valid retrieval (one SAR day near the February minimum); of these 89.8% are valid open-water zeros, and 100 % is the most frequent ice value. 295,054 fill cells lie inside SAR swaths (probable land/ice-shelf mask). No out-of-range values were found.

figures.name: fig07_dmi_sic_map
figures.title: DMI-ASIP sea-ice concentration map preview
figures.caption: Native polar-stereographic grid (true-scale latitude 70 S) subsampled every 8th cell for display only (no averaging). Grey = _FillValue (no SAR coverage or masked).
figures.interpretation: Valid retrievals are confined to the Sentinel-1 swaths acquired on 2023-02-02 (13:35-20:08 UTC); most of the Southern Ocean has no retrieval in this single daily file, so it cannot be used for circumpolar statistics without more days.

figures.name: fig08_glims_map
figures.title: GLIMS Antarctic glacier outlines
figures.caption: Glacier outlines (line_type = glac_bound) from the GLIMS download filtered to RGI first-order region 19, reprojected to EPSG:3031 for display only (stored data keep EPSG:4326). Coloured by the GLIMS geog_area attribute (top five + Other).
figures.interpretation: 15,280 outlines; coverage is concentrated on the Antarctic Peninsula (9,470) and peripheral islands, with very sparse coverage of the main ice sheet - GLIMS is a glacier (not ice-sheet) inventory.

figures.name: fig09_glims_area_hist
figures.title: GLIMS glacier area distribution
figures.caption: Histogram of the database-computed area (db_area, km^2) of RGI-19 glacier outlines with logarithmic bins.
figures.interpretation: Median area 0.03 km^2, maximum 165,079 km^2. Recomputed equal-area (EASE-Grid 2.0 South) areas match db_area with a median relative difference of 5.1e-07; 63 outlines differ by >5 % (of which 0 have invalid geometry) and are flagged for review, not removed.

figures.name: fig10_glims_hypsometry
figures.title: Aggregate glacier hypsometry
figures.caption: Sum over all RGI-19 glaciers with hypsometry of the glacier area in each 50 m elevation bin.
figures.interpretation: 3,100 glacier analyses, 145,016 km^2 in total; half of the area lies below about 282 m, and the highest populated bin is 3,575 m.

figures.name: fig11_pgc_tiles
figures.title: PGC/NCALM Dry Valleys LiDAR tile index
figures.caption: Tile footprints from the PGC-hosted KMZ index coloured by site (seven largest + Other) and the min-max elevation of each site.
figures.interpretation: 4,062 tiles in 13 sites with 14,126,743,483 LiDAR points in total; elevations span -59 to 2,930 m. Only the index is local - the LAS point clouds were not downloaded.

figures.name: fig12_missing_values
figures.title: Missing-value summary
figures.caption: Share of missing, null or _FillValue entries per dataset as computed by each handler (definitions differ by format: grid cells for rasters, attribute cells for vectors/tables, time steps for series).
figures.interpretation: Highest share: cmems_dmi_asip_sic (98.7%). For the DMI-ASIP grid this is fill outside SAR coverage and for hypsometry empty elevation bins - structural, not lost measurements. Time series: nsidc_g02135_south_daily 0.00%, cmems_omi_si_extent 0.72%.

figures.name: fig13_before_after_counts
figures.title: Before-and-after record counts
figures.caption: Records/features in the source versus the processed output. Reductions are scope subsets (Antarctic filter), never deletions of Antarctic observations; source files are unchanged.
figures.interpretation: Counts are preserved for all tabular and time-series datasets. Reductions occur only where a global source was subset to the Antarctic scope: glims_hypsometry (153,223 -> 3,100), glims_points (392,096 -> 11,280), glims_polygons (790,854 -> 15,358).

figures.name: fig14_edsc_providers
figures.title: Earthdata Search catalog providers
figures.caption: Number of catalog records per data provider in the Earthdata Search collection export (metadata only).
figures.interpretation: 97 collection records from 5 providers; 38 mention Antarctic operational modes or titles; 32 are ongoing (no end date). No science granules were downloaded.
